questions.q: The pressure $( P )$ and temperature $( T )$ relationship of an ideal gas obeys the equation $PT^{2} =$ constant. The volume expansion coefficient of the gas will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given here,

$PT^{2} =$constant~ $. . . \left(1\right)$

Using ideal gas equation,~

$PV = nRT$

We have,~$P = $\dfrac{nRT}{V}

Putting in equation~ \left(1\right)$,

$PT^{2} = $\dfrac{nRT}{V} \timesT^{2} =constant

$⇒ T^{3} = KV . . . \left(2\right)$

Differentiating the equation with respect to~$T$,~

So,~$\dfrac{d}{dT}\left(KV\right) = 3T^{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{KdV}{dT} =3T^{2}$

$⇒ dV = \dfrac{3T^{2}}{K}dT$

$⇒ \gammaV = \dfrac{3T^{2}}{K} \left(\text{as}dV = \gamma VdT\right)$

$⇒ \gamma = \dfrac{3T^{2}}{KV} = \dfrac{3T^{2}}{T3} = \dfrac{3}{T}$

$

questions.q:
Which statements are correct about degrees of freedom?

A. A molecule with $n$ degrees of freedom has $n^{2}$ different ways of storing energy.

B. Each degree of freedom is associated with $\dfrac{1}{2}RT$ average energy per mole.

C. A monoatomic gas molecule has $1$ rotational degree of freedom where as diatomic molecule has $2$ rotational degrees of freedom

D. ${CH}_{4}$ has a total to $6$ degrees of freedom.

Choose the correct answer from the option given below:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
According to the equipartition of energy, each degree of freedom carries& $\dfrac{1}{2}RT$~energy per mole and total energy per mole of a gas having~$n$~degrees of freedom is~$\dfrac{1}{2}nRT$. Therefore, statement A is wrong and statement B is correct.

A monoatomic molecule& only has translational degrees of freedom and does not have rotational degree of freedom. For a polyatomic model there are three rotational degrees of freedom and three translational degrees of freedom. Therefore, statement C is incorrect and statement D is correct.

questions.q: An unknown metal of mass $192g$ heated to a temperature of $100 ° C$ was immersed into a brass calorimeter of mass $128g$ containing $240g$ of water at a temperature of ${8.4}^{o}C .$ Calculate the specific heat of the unknown metal if water temperature stabilizes at ${21.5}^{o}C .($ Specific heat of brass is $394Jkg^{- 1}K^{- 1} )$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Conservation of energy:

$ms\Delta T = \left({m}_{b}{s}_{b} + {m}_{w}{s}_{w}\right)\Delta{T}_{w}$

$192 \times {10}^{- 3}s \left($100 - 21.5\right) = \left(128 \times394 + 240 \times4182\right)\times {10}^{- 3} \times\left($21.5 - 8.4\right)$

$s = $\dfrac{\left(50432 + 1003680\right)\left(13.1\right)}{15072} =$916 . 19 ≃ 916$~$Jkg^{- 1}K^{- 1}$

for gas $B$

$= \dfrac{3RT}{V} = \dfrac{3 \times 8 . 314 ( 400 )}{4 \times {10}^{- 3}} = 24 . 9 \times {10}^{5}Pa$

questions.q: If three moles of monoatomic gas  \left(\gamma = \dfrac{5}{3}\right)$ is mixed with two moles of a diatomic gas  \left(\gamma = \dfrac{7}{5}\right)$, the value of adiabatic exponent $\gamma$ for the mixture is:

questions.solution:
Given:

$\begin{cases}{f}_{1} = 3, & {f}_{2} = 5 \\ {n}_{1} = 3, & {n}_{2} = 2\end{cases}$

Now, for mixture

${f}_{mixture} = \dfrac{{n}_{1}{f}_{1} + {n}_{2}{f}_{2}}{{n}_{1} + {n}_{2}} = \dfrac{9 + 10}{5} = \dfrac{19}{5}$

Therefore, ${γ}_{mixture} = 1 + \dfrac{2}{f\text{mixture}} = 1 + \dfrac{2 \times 5}{19} = \dfrac{29}{19} = 1 . 52$

questions.q: When heat $Q$ is supplied to a diatomic gas of rigid molecules, at constant volume its temperature increases by $∆ T$ . The heat required to produce the same change in temperature, at a constant pressure is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For diatomic gas ${C}_{P} = \dfrac{7}{2}R$
${C}_{V} = \dfrac{5}{2}R$
Heat supplied at constant volume $Q = n{C}_{V}\Delta T$
Heat supplied at constant pressure $Q^{'} = n{C}_{P}\Delta T$
$\dfrac{Q}{Q^{'}} = \dfrac{{C}_{V}}{{C}_{P}}$
$Q^{'} = Q\dfrac{CP}{CV} = \dfrac{7}{5}Q$ ~

questions.q: A mixture of hydrogen and oxygen has volume $500{cm}^{3},$~temperature $300K,$~pressure $400$ kPa and mass $0 . 76g .$ The ratio of masses of oxygen to hydrogen will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
A number of moles of,& ${O}_{2} = \dfrac{m1}{32}$, the number of moles of,~${H}_{2} = \dfrac{m2}{2}$. Using the ideal gas equation,~$PV = \left[\dfrac{m1}{32} + \dfrac{m2}{2}\right]\dfrac{25}{3} \times 300$,~
$400 \times {10}^{3} \times 500 \times {10}^{- 6} = \left[\dfrac{m1}{32} + \dfrac{m2}{2}\right]25 \times 100 ⇒ 2 \times {10}^{2} = \left[\dfrac{m1}{m2} \times \dfrac{1}{32} + \dfrac{1}{2}\right]{m}_{2} \times 25 \times 100$
$⇒ \dfrac{2}{25} = \left[\dfrac{m1}{m2} \times \dfrac{1}{32} + \dfrac{1}{2}\right]{m}_{2} . . . ( 1 )$~ ~
$⇒ {m}_{1} + {m}_{2} = 0 . 76$
$⇒ {m}_{2}\left[1 + \dfrac{m1}{m2}\right] = \dfrac{76}{100} . . . ( 2 )$~
$( 1 )$ divided by $( 2 )$ ;~\left[\dfrac{m1}{m2} \times \dfrac{1}{32} + \dfrac{1}{2}\right]\left[\dfrac{m1}{m2} + 1\right] = \dfrac{2}{25} \times \dfrac{100}{76}$
Let assume,~
$⇒ \dfrac{m1}{m2} = x ⇒ \dfrac{x + 16}{32\left[x + 1\right]} = \dfrac{8}{76} ⇒ 76x + 76 \times 16 = 8 \times 32x + 8 \times 32 ⇒ 76x + 1216 = 256x + 256$
$960 = 180x ⇒ x = \dfrac{96}{18} = \dfrac{16}{3}$ /$

questions.q:
Nitrogen gas is at $300 ° C$ temperature. The temperature (in $K$ ) at which the rms speed of a ${H}_{2}$ molecule would be equal to the rms speed of a nitrogen molecule, is $\ldots \ldots \ldots .$~(Molar mass of ${N}_{2}$ gas $28g$ ).
&
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given,

Temperature of Nitrogen gas is&

${T}_{1} = 300 ° C = 300 + 273 = 573K$

Molar mass of~${H}_{2}$~gas is ${M}_{H2} = 2g$

Molar mass of ${N}_{2}$ gas is~${M}_{N2} = 28g$

The rms speed of gas is given by

~${V}_{rms} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{M}}$

Now rms speed of hydrogen gas is equal to rms speed of nitrogen gas, i.e.;~\left({V}_{rms}\right){H}_{2} = \left({V}_{rms}\right){N}_{2}$
$⇒ \dfrac{T{H}_{2}}{T{N}_{2}} = \dfrac{M{H}_{2}}{M{N}_{2}}$

Substitute the given values i above equation, we get,

${T}_{H2} = \dfrac{2}{28} \times 573$

${T}_{H2} = 41K$

$

questions.q:
A monoatomic gas performs a work of $\dfrac{Q}{4}$ where $Q$ is the heat supplied to it. The molar heat capacity of the gas will be _____~$R$ during this transformation.

Where $R$ is the gas constant.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Using first law of thermodynamics,

$Q = ∆ U + W$

$⇒ Q = \Delta U + \dfrac{Q}{4}$

$⇒ \Delta U = \dfrac{3Q}{4}$

$⇒ ∆ U = \dfrac{3}{2}nR\Delta T = \dfrac{3Q}{4}$

Therefore, molar heat capacity,~$C = \dfrac{Q}{n ∆ T}$

$⇒ C = 2R$
